name: The morphological scale (faʿala)
definition: The pattern فَعَلَ, whose letters fāʾ, ʿayn and lām stand for the first, second and third root letters of any word.
body: To describe the form of a word, ṣarf weighs it against فعل. نَصَرَ is on the pattern فَعَلَ: its nūn is the fāʾ, its ṣād the ʿayn, its rāʾ the lām. يَنْصُرُ is on the pattern يَفْعُلُ, and نَاصِرٌ on فَاعِلٌ.

Letters added to the root appear in the pattern as they are: أَكْرَمَ is أَفْعَلَ, and اِسْتَغْفَرَ is اِسْتَفْعَلَ. So the scale shows at a glance which letters belong to the root and which were added.

examples.text: naṣara is on the pattern faʿala.
istaghfara is on the pattern istafʿala: the alif, sīn and tāʾ are added.
